newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD consortia due to register Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD consortia due to register Thursday.

text.p: The two consortia likely to bid in the privatization auction of Brazilian state mining giant CVRD have until 1600 local time/1900 GMT Thursday to register with the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange clearing house.

They will have to present a list of members and financial guarantees for 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion) among other documents in order to qualify for the April 29 sale of a 40-45-percent voting stake in CVRD.
A base price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion) has been set for the share block.
Spokesmen for the consortia said they would be engaged in negotiations with further potential partners until the last minute, but their basic constellation is already clear.

Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South African mining conglomerate Anglo-American Corp are leading one of the consortia, named Valecom, while Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN is leading the other.

Votorantim and Anglo-American have equal stakes in Valecom which amount to more than 50 percent jointly, while a group of 12 Japanese steelmakers and trading companies led by Nippon Steel Corp has a 10-percent stake in Valecom.

The group of Japanese investors comprises Nippon Steel Corp, NKK Corp, Kawasaki Steel Corp, Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd, Kobe Steel Ltd, Nisshin Steel Co Ltd, Nakayama Steel Works Ltd, Nissho Iwai Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Corp, Itochu Corp and Marubeni Corp.

Brazilian metal and metallurgical group Caemi, 40-percent-owned by Japan's Mitsui & Co, has also joined Valecom as have two Brazilian pension funds, Centrus and Sistel, which have an existing joint stake in CVRD of 2.8 percent.
Brazilian bank Banco Safra has also been cited as a possible member of Valecom.

CSN has joined ranks with South African mining firm Gencor, likely to hold a 10-percent stake in the consortium, and Nations Bank which is expected to contribute $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion to the consortium.

Opportunity Asset Management, an offshore investment fund for foreign mainly U.S. investors, has also teamed up with CSN, as have Brazilian pulp and paper group Suzano and four Brazilian pension funds, Previ, Petros, Funcef and Funcesp.
The pension funds already have a joint voting stake in CVRD of 10.03 percent, which would give the CSN consortium a controling position in CVRD if it wins the auction.
Brazilian construction firm Camargo Correia and U.S. aluminium company Alcoa have also been in talks with CSN and may still join the consortium.
